title: Defining a clinical protocol using a computerized central visual processing battery
author: Costa, Henriques, et al.

steps.title: Configure staircase parameters
steps.instruction: Set the staircase to target 79.4 % correct with a total of six reversals per subtest. For the first two reversals reduce stimulus magnitude by 50 %; for the next four reversals reduce by 12.5 %. After any error increase the stimulus value of the next trial by 25 %. Use asymmetric step sizes as described.

steps.title: Define constant‑method settings
steps.instruction: For all subtests using the constant‑stimulus method present each stimulus level for seven judgments (7 repetitions) to allow reliable psychometric fitting.

steps.title: Prepare linear grating contrast stimulus
steps.instruction: Create a linear grating with Gabor envelope, size 4°, presentation time 5 s. Use spatial frequencies 0.4, 1.6, 3.2, 6.4 and 12.8 cpd. Apply the staircase method with six reversals.

steps.title: Prepare radial grating contrast stimulus
steps.instruction: Create a radial grating identical to the linear grating (size 4°, Gabor envelope, 5 s, SF 0.4‑12.8 cpd) and run a six‑reversal staircase.

steps.title: Prepare temporal contrast stimulus
steps.instruction: Generate a luminance‑modulated Gabor (size 4°, 5 s) with temporal frequencies 2.0, 8.0, 18.0 and 24.0 Hz. Use a six‑reversal staircase.

steps.title: Prepare second‑order texture stimulus
steps.instruction: Display a linear grating on a pink‑noise carrier, size 4°, Gabor envelope, spatial frequencies 0.4, 1.6, 3.2 and 6.4 cpd. Use a six‑reversal staircase.

steps.title: Prepare coherent motion stimulus
steps.instruction: Show 50 dots each 0.3° moving coherently left or right. Dot permanence 100 ms (initial) then 1000 ms. Motion speeds 2°/s and 10°/s. Use a six‑reversal staircase.

steps.title: Prepare line‑bisection stimulus
steps.instruction: Draw a horizontal line 15° long with a black marker 0.1° wide. Position the marker at –0.60°, –0.45°, –0.20°, 0.0°, 0.20°, 0.45° and 0.60°. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare form‑detection (colinear) stimulus
steps.instruction: Present a linear grating (3.5 cpd, size 0.5°) within circles of 4° and 7° diameter, surrounded by 30 distractors of random orientation. Include 6‑20 collinear elements. Apply a six‑reversal staircase.

steps.title: Prepare form‑distortion stimulus
steps.instruction: Show a radial circle 4° in diameter with thickness 0.1° or 0.3°. Apply radial deformities of 5 dpc and 10 dpc. Use a six‑reversal staircase.

steps.title: Prepare form‑discrimination stimulus
steps.instruction: Create 24 geometric figure distractors (size 1°) with 6‑10 sides and one target figure (size 1°) of either 6 or 10 sides. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare subjective time perception stimulus
steps.instruction: Display circles (1° radius) at 5° left and right. Target durations: 0.8 s, 1.2 s, 1.6 s, 2.1 s; reference duration 1.0 s. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare automatic attention stimulus
steps.instruction: Show a linear grating (3.5 cpd, size 0.5°) oriented 90°. Include 99 distractors; the target is oriented 100°, 110° or 125°. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare sustained attention stimulus
steps.instruction: Present 1° bars for 3 s. Black bars at 0° and 90°, white bars at 90°. The target is one white bar at 0°. Distractor counts: 21, 35 or 50. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare quantitative estimation stimulus
steps.instruction: Reference: 40 dots (0.3° each) covering a 4° area on the left side. Target: 15, 25, 30 or 38 dots on the right side. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare mental number line stimulus
steps.instruction: Draw a horizontal line 30° long, 1° thick, representing a 0‑10 scale. Test numbers: 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9. Record mouse x‑position freely. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare saccadic planning stimulus
steps.instruction: Use syllable references (ZU, MA, VI, TA, LO) and targets (SA, PA, BA, NA, RA, DA, FA). First central fixation 120 ms, second central fixation 120 ms (total 240 ms). Eccentricities: 0.4°, 2.0° and 6.8°. Use the constant‑stimulus method with seven judgments.

steps.title: Prepare rapid automated naming stimulus
steps.instruction: Select 7 numbers randomly from 0‑9. Present each for 500 ms, 950 ms and 1400 ms across three trials. Record reaction time mean.

steps.title: Randomize subtest order
steps.instruction: For each participant, generate a random sequence of the above subtests using the predefined randomization table before testing begins.

steps.title: Run each subtest and collect responses
steps.instruction: Present the stimuli according to the parameters defined for each subtest, record the participant’s response on every trial, and adjust stimulus intensity on staircase tasks using the configured step‑size rules.

steps.title: Fit psychometric functions
steps.instruction: For all constant‑stimulus subtests, fit a psychometric function to the seven‑judgment data to estimate the threshold corresponding to 79.4 % correct.

steps.title: Derive thresholds and store data
steps.instruction: Extract the 79.4 % correct threshold from each fitted function (or from the final reversal of staircase tasks) and save all raw and processed data for later analysis.

description: The validation of the protocol was analysed through replicability and reliability measures and split-half correlation, based on pilot data collected from 41 healthy adult participants. These participants were recruited by convenience sampling from among students and staff at the University of São Paulo, with a mean age of 20 years (SD = 2 years), 22 females. Replicability was analyzed using a test–retest procedure for all 41 participants. The retest was conducted after a minimum interval of two weeks (mean = 22 days, SD = 5 days). The order of the subtests was randomized for each participant, based on a predefined randomization table. The analysis of variance revealed no statistically significant differences between the first and second assessments for any of the subtests evaluated (p > 0.05), with a large effect size indicated by eta squared (η² = 0.417).
